I am 49 years old and have farmed these 7.8 mu in Quzhou for 30 years. I know every corner of this land. With six people in my household and my sons working off-farm in the city, I must be careful with labor. I cannot manage too much cotton because picking it by hand takes time we do not have. So I will keep 5 mu in my reliable wheat-maize double crop and 2.8 mu in cotton. The wheat is already in the ground from last October, and that is fine.

For the winter wheat, I will top-dress urea at green-up in March because the base fertilizer I put down in autumn is not enough to carry it to harvest. I will irrigate four times total—return-green, jointing, heading, and grain-filling—since my well gives me water and I do not trust the spring rains alone. Three sprays will deal with weeds and aphids. I use an improved Jimai variety; it is not the newest seed on the market, but it is steady and I know how it behaves on my soil.

After wheat harvest in early June, I will immediately rotary-till and plant hybrid maize. The turnaround must be fast. I will apply compound fertilizer at sowing and side-dress nitrogen at the big-flush stage. Summer maize usually gets some rain, so two irrigations at jointing and filling will be enough if the skies cooperate. Two sprays—one herbicide, one for corn borer.

For cotton, I will plant Bt hybrid seed in late April after rotary tillage. I will lay plastic mulch to keep moisture and suppress weeds; this saves me labor later. I will fertilize at planting and top-dress at flowering. Three irrigations and four pesticide applications will see it through, even though the Bt gene helps with bollworm. I expect about 100 kg of lint per mu, which is decent for my ground.

I do not do no-tillage. I tried it once and the soil got too hard and weedy. Rotary tillage works for me.
